story.iWant: screenshots to be automatically captured when window changes occur
story.soThat: I don't have to manually take screenshots during documentation

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given a documentation session is active, when the active window changes or a significant UI event occurs, then a screenshot is automatically captured
Given a screenshot has been captured, then the screenshot is stored with a unique identifier (UUID format)
Given a screenshot has been captured, then the screenshot is associated with the current session step
Given a screenshot has been captured, then the screenshot metadata (timestamp, window title) is recorded
Given a window change is detected, then screenshot capture completes within 100ms of window change detection

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: Automatically capture screenshots when window changes are detected. Monitor active window changes, capture screenshots using mss/pywinctl, store screenshots with unique identifiers, associate screenshots with session steps.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: ScreenshotCapture handles all screenshot operations. Uses mss for cross-platform support, pywinctl for window-specific capture. Screenshots stored with unique identifiers, associated with session steps.

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Window change detection and monitoring, screenshot capture using mss/pywinctl, screenshot storage with unique identifiers, screenshot metadata recording (timestamp, window title). Performance target: capture within 100ms.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: Foundation story with no prerequisites. Use ScreenshotCapture class in src/capture/screenshot.py, implement window monitoring via src/monitor/window_monitor.py, use mss/pywinctl for cross-platform screenshot capture.

artifact.reason: Existing ScreenshotCapture class implements screenshot capture functionality. Already supports Windows and cross-platform capture using mss/pywinctl. Needs enhancement for UUID-based naming and metadata recording.

Existing WindowMonitor class implements window change detection. Uses polling mechanism with callback support. Already integrated with SessionManager. May need performance optimization for 100ms target.

SessionManager orchestrates screenshot capture via WindowMonitor callback. Already integrates ScreenshotCapture and WindowMonitor. Needs enhancement for UUID-based screenshot IDs and metadata storage in session steps.
Structured logging utility used throughout codebase. Follow ADR-009 for logging standards.
Existing unit tests for ScreenshotCapture. Need to add tests for UUID-based naming and metadata recording.
Existing unit tests for WindowMonitor. Need to add performance tests for 100ms capture time requirement.
Integration tests for screenshot workflow. Need to add tests for complete workflow: window change → screenshot capture → storage → metadata.

constraint.rule: Layered Architecture: Screenshot capture belongs to Capture Layer (src/capture/), window monitoring belongs to Monitor Layer (src/monitor/)
ScreenshotCapture should not directly access GUI components; communication via SessionManager
Use exception-based error handling with comprehensive logging (ADR-008)
Screenshot capture must complete within 100ms to meet PRD requirements
Screenshots stored in data/screenshots/{session_id}/ directory structure

interface.name: ScreenshotCapture.capture_window
interface.signature: def capture_window(self, hwnd: Optional[int] = None, step_number: Optional[int] = None, max_retries: int = 2) -> Optional[Path]
interface.description: Captures screenshot of a window. Returns path to screenshot file or None on error.

interface.name: ScreenshotCapture.capture_screen
interface.signature: def capture_screen(self, step_number: Optional[int] = None) -> Optional[Path]
interface.description: Captures screenshot of entire screen. Returns path to screenshot file or None on error.

interface.name: WindowMonitor.start_monitoring
interface.description: Starts window monitoring in background thread. Calls callback on window change.

interface.name: WindowMonitor.stop_monitoring
interface.description: Stops window monitoring and joins thread.

interface.name: WindowMonitor._get_window_info
interface.description: Extracts window information including title, class name, dimensions. Returns dict with window metadata.

interface.name: SessionManager._on_window_change
interface.description: Callback method called by WindowMonitor on window change. Triggers screenshot capture and step creation.

interface.name: SessionManager._capture_current_step
interface.description: Captures current step including screenshot, OCR, and AI generation. Creates session step with metadata.

tests.standards: Use pytest with pytest-mock for mocking external dependencies. Unit tests for individual components, integration tests for complete workflow. Performance tests to verify 100ms capture time requirement. Error handling tests for all error scenarios. Target 80% code coverage minimum.

test.description: Test ScreenshotCapture metadata recording (timestamp, window title)
Test WindowMonitor window change detection performance (100ms target)
Test complete workflow: window change → screenshot capture → storage → metadata
Verify screenshot capture completes within 100ms of window change detection
Test screenshot capture failures, storage failures, window monitoring errors
Test multiple rapid window changes handled correctly
